upstream.process: Hepatic mitochondrial ketogenesis proceeds through acetoacetyl-CoA formation, HMG-CoA synthase and HMG-CoA lyase to produce acetoacetate.
dependencies: Ketone release, circulation and brain monocarboxylate transport
upstream.limitations: The endogenous product can interconvert with beta-hydroxybutyrate, but the target identity here is acetoacetate. Ketogenesis, cerebral uptake and ATP production are distinct; no fixed yield or universal benefit is inferred.

evidence.statement: Curated human ACAT1, HMGCS2 and HMGCL reactions, retrieved 26 October 2026.

inventory.name: Acetyl-CoA
inventory.reason: Canonical precursor/conversion or shared parent identity retained; no independently resolved eligible target relationship

upstream.process: Hepatic fatty-acid activation and successive mitochondrial beta-oxidation reactions generate acetyl-CoA from the C8 chain.
upstream.limitations: This is a multireaction biological process, not a single chemical reaction. Tissue partitioning and energy state prevent a fixed food-to-acetyl-CoA yield. Cofactor participation creates no separate dietary admissions.

evidence.statement: Human medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase establishes the initial beta-oxidation reaction; the clinical exposure additionally measures downstream ketone provision.

records.limitation: Protein-quality scoring and vegetarian-diet amino-acid coverage do not establish that increasing protein raises brain monoamine synthesis or improves attention or mood. The indispensable set includes phenylalanine; tyrosine is not an indispensable amino acid.

Dietary supply to a circulating pool is distinct from brain transport, catecholamine synthesis or clinical benefit. A small human study found higher plasma tyrosine during protein-containing meals and after a large tyrosine supplement; it does not define ordinary-food efficacy or a need for extra tyrosine when supply is adequate. Tyrosine is not an indispensable amino acid.
Competitive transport biology does not establish that eating more tyrosine increases brain tyrosine or catecholamine signalling.
Substrate necessity does not establish that additional dietary tyrosine increases brain dopamine or improves a functional or clinical outcome.

Tyrosine is upstream precursor supply, not the immediate DBH substrate or an independently adjudicated Direct dietary requirement here. Ordinary dietary competitive changes do not establish a limiting effect on regional noradrenergic signalling or benefit from extra tyrosine.
Pool presence of tryptophan is not evidence for increased brain serotonin, brain entry, or an attention or mood benefit.
Meal-driven changes in plasma tryptophan-to-LNAA ratios do not establish increased brain serotonin or a clinical benefit.
Substrate necessity does not establish that additional dietary tryptophan increases brain serotonin or improves mood, sleep or ADHD.
Human intake-to-dopamine responsiveness and clinical benefit were not established; the direct dopamine-metabolite evidence assessed here is preclinical deficiency evidence.
Human intake-to-noradrenaline responsiveness and clinical benefit were not established; the cited dopamine-metabolite and developmental evidence is not a noradrenaline-dosing trial.
Iron is required by the hydroxylase. That is not evidence that extra dietary iron raises brain serotonin when iron status is adequate.
Evidence supports improved non-haem iron absorption at the meal level; it does not establish improved iron status or any change in dopamine biology or function.

Methionine is required to enter the cycle. This does not show that raising methionine intake increases human remethylation or transsulfuration rates.

A formula that removed methionine and cysteine together slowed whole-blood synthesis, so that result does not isolate methionine. In the cysteine-free study, methionine intake stayed adequate and red-cell synthesis did not fall. This does not show that eating more methionine, once intake is adequate, raises glutathione synthesis.

Endogenous remethylation also supplies methionine. Neonatal-piglet isotope incorporation does not establish an adult intake target, cerebral delivery or benefit above adequacy. Methyl allocation, SAH inhibition, transport and other substrate availability constrain the route; no shared KC admission follows.

Human MAT structural and enzymological evidence establishes catalytic capacity. Ordinary food supply is distinct from measured MAT flux; no benefit from additional magnesium in replete people or universal methylation increase is asserted.

Human GSS crystallography and cofactor annotation support capacity. The structure contains two magnesium ions; this does not establish a dietary dose, increased blood or neuronal glutathione synthesis, or benefit above adequacy. Original one-per-subunit wording is retained in history rather than used as dietary stoichiometry.

Human MAT structures establish the specific ion relationship. Physiological potassium homeostasis and tissue uptake intervene; no claim that extra dietary potassium raises SAM flux or improves methylation is established.

In nine healthy young adults, 28 days of vitamin B6 restriction lowered plasma pyridoxal phosphate and did not change mean postprandial remethylation, transmethylation, or total transsulfuration rates.

Salvage of food vitamin B6 to pyridoxal 5'-phosphate does not show that higher vitamin B6 intake increases cystathionine beta-synthase or cystathionine gamma-lyase flux. Moderate B6 restriction changed cystathionine handling but did not significantly reduce total transsulfuration in the assessed human tracer study.

Endogenous glycine synthesis and other methyltransferases also contribute. Enzyme loss is not glycine deficiency; extra dietary glycine has not been established to normalise whole-cycle or brain methylation.
In older adults glycine was supplemented together with a cysteine precursor, so that rise in erythrocyte synthesis does not isolate glycine.

Purified-enzyme dependence on pyridoxal 5'-phosphate does not show that raising vitamin B6 intake increases cysteine formation in people. Moderate B6 restriction changed cystathionine handling but did not significantly reduce total transsulfuration in the assessed human tracer study.
Serine is a direct enzyme substrate. Endogenous synthesis and diet can both supply it; this does not show that dietary serine or protein intake increases cystathionine formation.

Cysteine is the substrate of the first assembly step. A formula that removed methionine and cysteine together slowed whole-blood synthesis, and that formula also removed methionine. When methionine intake stayed adequate, removing cysteine did not lower red-cell synthesis in young men. This does not show that eating more cysteine, once intake is adequate, raises glutathione synthesis.
No human study in this assessment showed that changing dietary glutamate changes glutathione synthesis.

The synthesis increase was measured in older adults given this precursor together with glycine. It does not show an effect of N-acetylcysteine alone, of ordinary foods, or of supplementation outside that group, and it is not a neuronal or clinical result.
Plasma tracing does not measure absolute hepatic flux, intermediary SAM, ordinary-food equivalence or benefit.

Uridine is a supported precursor source, not an indispensable dietary requirement: endogenous nucleotide synthesis and salvage also supply CTP. Rat-slice and oral-UMP gerbil results do not establish an ordinary-food dose, increased human PC flux or cognitive benefit; human MRS measures precursor pools.

Reviewed UniProt IKBKB records the ATP-dependent IκB kinase reaction without a magnesium cofactor annotation; published IKKβ crystals used in this review are inhibitor-bound rather than ATP–Mg ternary complexes. This does not establish that ordinary dietary magnesium intake limits human NF-κB transcription.

Cellular redox studies show context-dependent effects, including inhibition after glutathione depletion or increased extracellular cysteine. Neither individual dietary limitation, brain transfer nor benefit from additional intake is established.

In Salmonella-infected rats, glutathione depletion did not increase permeability or bacterial translocation. Neither intestinal precursor inadequacy, individual constituent limitation, human LPS reduction nor benefit from additional intake is established.

Human target engagement varies by formulation, tissue and population. The positive study used a myrosinase-completed broccoli sprout homogenate for three days in healthy nonsmokers and measured nasal phase II enzyme RNA, not Nrf2 protein or nuclear translocation. Extract capsules did not increase lung target-gene expression in COPD. An ordinary broccoli meal, direct activation of Nrf2 in the human brain and clinical ADHD benefit remain unestablished. Sulforaphane is not an essential nutrient.

In selenium-deficient adults, plasma glutathione peroxidase activity levelled off once intake reached about 35 micrograms a day. Intake above that plateau did not raise the enzyme further, and the study did not measure net oxidative pressure.

Mouse whole-organ enzyme assays do not identify mitochondrial isoforms, a human food dose or benefit above selenium adequacy. Repletion response depended on dose; antioxidant capacity does not establish clinical prevention.
Culture selenium exposure is not an oral food dose. This supports the thioredoxin arm, not selenium dependence of glutathione reductase, universal tissue recycling flux or benefit above adequacy.

Curated human SOD1 and experimental structural evidence support a structural capacity relationship, not zinc-dependent catalysis identical to copper. Erythrocyte superoxide dismutase rose after copper repletion in infants with marginal copper status. That does not show that extra copper raises the enzyme when status is already adequate.

Human SOD2 requires manganese; dietary depletion experiments measured lower heart and kidney MnSOD activity in rats. This establishes a bounded enzyme-capacity dependency, not a human dose recommendation, universal tissue response, measured net ROS balance or benefit above adequate intake.

Rat diet and tissue context; the kidney result is not a uniform response across organs or a human intake threshold. Human catalase haem identity supports capacity, not benefit from extra iron. Iron can also promote non-enzymatic oxidation; higher catalase activity is not a clinical benefit.

Vitamin E breaks peroxyl-radical chains in membranes. That chemistry does not show that extra vitamin E lowers peroxidation in people. A prevention trial found more prostate cancers with 400 IU a day.
Regeneration of the vitamin E radical is not a high-dose rule. A prevention trial found more prostate cancers with 400 IU of vitamin E a day.

Glutamine is supplied substantially from endogenous and systemic pools and becomes conditionally indispensable under stress; adult supplementation trials show no overall permeability benefit, so dietary protein or glutamine provision is not established as a general PM1 lever. 106 completers from115 randomised; narrative withdrawal counts are internally inconsistent. Use flow/Results cohort sizes, not a claim of complete intention-to-treat. Not generalisable to IBS with normal permeability, other disease types, children, pregnancy/lactation or excluded renal/hepatic impairment. No significant control-arm permeability change; adverse-event rates similar and no serious adverse events reported. Long-term safety not established. Earlier discovery shorthand0.05 versus0.11 conflated post-treatment with active-group baseline; post-treatment control was0.10, and Table3 is the actual between-group change comparison.

Coordinate peripheral metabolic clock timing through feeding cues.
Enable NAPE-to-NAE biosynthesis so endocannabinoidome signalling lipids remain available for stress and motivation regulation.
Sustain omega-3-derived ethanolamide production so endocannabinoidome neuromodulation stays supplied from dietary fat status.
Preserve endocannabinoid signalling duration by limiting FAAH-mediated degradation of anandamide and related NAEs.
Shape dopaminergic reward and motivation pathways through endocannabinoid neuromodulatory interaction.
Sustain endocannabinoid-mediated stress buffering so HPA-axis and neuroinflammatory reactivity stay proportionate.
Maintain stable oestrogen-linked signalling so dopamine tone and emotional regulation remain steady across hormonal fluctuation.
Shape systemic oestrogen exposure through microbiome-mediated regulation of oestrogen metabolism and recycling.
Sustain microbial contributions to progesterone-related hormonal stability through gut ecosystem function.
Enable coordinated integration of insulin and metabolic signalling with reproductive hormone balance.
Maintain androgen receptor signalling so motivation, stamina, and goal-directed effort remain well supported.
Shape systemic androgen exposure through microbiome-mediated androgen metabolism and recycling.
Ensure meal-level protein supply delivers the amino-acid foundation neurotransmitter pathways depend on.
Regulate competitive transport of large neutral amino acids across the blood–brain barrier in response to circulating substrate availability.
Maintain appropriately regulated dopamine synthesis, storage, release, receptor signalling, reuptake and metabolism across changing functional demand.
Support noradrenergic alertness and executive control so attention and arousal stay appropriately engaged.
Support serotonergic signalling so mood stability, inhibition, and behavioural regulation remain well grounded.
Maintain the capacity to form acetylcholine so cholinergic signalling for attention, working memory, and learning stays supplied.
Deliver and integrate DHA into neuronal membranes so the brain maintains a flexible, signal-ready lipid foundation.
Clear and recycle glutamate efficiently so excitatory load does not overwhelm neural circuits.
Limit excitotoxic pressure when glutamatergic drive is excessive so neural stability is protected over time.
Maintain sufficient glutamate decarboxylase capacity, and sufficient PLP cofactor to support it, so GABA can be synthesised from glutamate.
Maintain and adapt physical connections between neurons through synapse formation, selective stabilisation, structural remodelling and elimination.
Recycle homocysteine to methionine through folate and B12 so methyl-donor supply and homocysteine control stay supported.
Provide a parallel homocysteine clearance route so methionine and SAMe supply remain resilient when folate demand is high.
Maintain methionine adenosyltransferase capacity to convert methionine and ATP into SAMe, sustaining the methyl-donor pool used by downstream methyltransferases.
Maintain balanced methionine-cycle flux so methionine availability, SAM-dependent methylation, homocysteine recycling and transsulfuration remain coordinated across changing physiological demand.
Divert homocysteine toward cysteine so methylation demand is balanced against sulfur amino-acid and redox needs.
Build glutathione from sulfur amino acids so cellular antioxidant defence stays connected to one-carbon metabolism.
Maintain phosphatidylcholine formation through PEMT methylation and the choline-based Kennedy pathway.
Regulate NF-κB transcriptional tone so pro-inflammatory gene programmes do not fire excessively.
Limit gut-derived endotoxin spillover so barrier dysfunction does not drive systemic inflammatory load.
Regulate the expression of cellular defence genes in response to oxidative and electrophilic stress.
Balance reactive oxygen species production and clearance so net oxidative pressure stays within tolerable limits.
Protect membrane fats from oxidative damage so vulnerable polyunsaturated fatty acids remain intact.
Regenerate vitamin and thiol antioxidants across networked systems so endogenous defence capacity is sustained.
Tune downstream cytokine signalling intensity so inflammatory tone does not remain chronically elevated.
Shift lipid mediator balance from pro-inflammatory eicosanoids toward pro-resolving signals that terminate inflammation.
Sustain efficient electron transport so mitochondria generate ATP without excessive electron leakage.
Maintain endogenous Coenzyme Q synthesis, maturation and pool availability to support mitochondrial electron transfer and cellular redox functions.
Maintain NAD⁺ availability so redox reactions and mitochondrial signalling stay adequately powered.
Enable rapid ATP buffering so high-energy-demand tissues can meet sudden metabolic spikes.
Regulate mitochondrial superoxide and hydrogen peroxide generation in response to metabolic conditions, preserving physiological redox signalling while limiting excessive oxidant production.
Preserve mitochondrial membrane and protein integrity through local protective mechanisms that limit oxidative injury and maintain organelle function.
Enable long-chain fatty-acid transport into mitochondria so fat-derived ATP production can proceed.
Enable mitochondrial ketone utilisation so alternative fuel is available when glucose conditions shift.
Shape smooth transitions between glucose, fat, and ketone fuel pathways as physiological demand shifts.
Enable formation of new mitochondria so long-term energetic capacity can expand and adapt.
Maintain epithelial tight junction integrity and selective permeability at the gut lining.
Limit host exposure to bacterial endotoxin and related inflammatory microbial products.
Support intestinal mucus maintenance and mucosal immune regulation through defined microbial activities.
Adjust community substrate-processing capacity through resource competition and changes in microbial function.
Maintain short-chain fatty acid production and signalling that supports gut barrier and brain communication.
Enable microbial activation of dietary polyphenols into bioactive metabolites.
Maintain gut-to-brain nerve signalling through the vagus nerve and enteric nervous system.
Maintain gut-side processing that shapes neurotransmitter precursor availability.
Shape the rate of post-meal glucose appearance so metabolic and neuroendocrine systems face manageable, predictable load.
Limit glycaemic volatility so post-prandial glucose swings do not create unnecessary metabolic and neuroendocrine stress.
Sustain insulin-sensitive glucose disposal so post-meal glucose clears efficiently without prolonged metabolic strain.
Maintain diurnal cortisol amplitude and phase so morning activation and evening downshift stay well timed.
Maintain autonomic flexibility by shifting cleanly from sympathetic activation back into parasympathetic recovery.
Sustain vagal tone so heart-rate-variability-linked recovery signalling remains robust under repeated stress exposure.
Regulate adipose-derived endocrine signalling and local glucocorticoid responsiveness to communicate metabolic state and coordinate hormonal adaptation.
Coordinate stress-responsive hypothalamic and reward signalling to regulate appetite and food-seeking motivation as physiological demands change.

transformations.process: MAT1A/MAT2A catalyse ATP-dependent methionine adenosylation to form SAM.
transformations.limitations: Reaction identity establishes capacity, not a universal limiting intake or greater flux from additional intake.

evidence.statement: Human MAT crystallography and curated Rhea 21080; P31153 v237 and Q00266 v233.

transformations.process: Riboflavin kinase (RFK) phosphorylates riboflavin to FMN using ATP.
transformations.limitations: Enzyme identity does not quantify tissue cofactor supply or flux after a meal.

evidence.statement: Human RFK catalyses riboflavin phosphorylation; UniProt Q969G6 entry 195 retrieved 2026-10-26, Rhea 14357.

transformations.process: FLAD1 FAD synthase adenylates FMN with ATP to form FAD.
transformations.limitations: FAD production and enzyme loading depend on cellular context; no fixed food-to-FAD yield is inferred.

evidence.statement: Human FLAD1 catalyses FMN adenylation; UniProt Q8NFF5 entry 182 retrieved 2026-10-26, Rhea 17237.

transformations.process: Human NRK1 phosphorylates beta-NR to beta-NMN using ATP.
transformations.limitations: An established intracellular route is not proof that all oral NR reaches each tissue intact; parallel degradation/salvage can contribute.

evidence.statement: NRK1 curated reaction, entry version 170, Rhea 14017, retrieved 26 October 2026.

transformations.process: NMN adenylyltransferase adenylates oxidised beta-NMN with ATP to form oxidised NAD.
transformations.limitations: NMNAT1 establishes reaction identity; other isoforms/transport determine compartmental provision. No fixed dietary conversion yield or mitochondrial/brain endpoint is inferred.

evidence.statement: Human NMNAT1, entry version 202, Rhea 21360, retrieved 26 October 2026.

transformations.process: Human AGAT transfers the amidino group of arginine to glycine, yielding guanidinoacetate and ornithine.
transformations.limitations: Both co-substrates are required; this is not a fixed dietary yield or an assertion that extra intake is rate-limiting.

evidence.statement: UniProt P50440 entry version 227, Rhea 13201; human renal GAA production independently measured.

transformations.process: GAMT methylates guanidinoacetate using S-adenosylmethionine to form creatine.
dependencies: Interorgan exchange and receiving-tissue creatine transport
transformations.limitations: Reaction identity does not prove dietary precursor limitation or cerebral delivery; SAM participation creates no independent methionine admission.

evidence.statement: UniProt Q14353 entry version 215, Rhea 10656.

transformations.process: Digestive lipolysis releases C8 fatty acid from trioctanoin; the absorbed fatty acid is represented as octanoate at physiological pH.
transformations.limitations: The C8 acyl form is not free octanoate content in food. Mixed-chain MCT products have formulation-dependent composition.

evidence.statement: Human triglyceride-lipase reaction provenance and the defined oral tricaprylin exposure; retrieved 26 October 2026.

transformations.process: Hepatic fatty-acid activation and successive mitochondrial beta-oxidation reactions generate acetyl-CoA from the C8 chain.
transformations.limitations: This is a multireaction biological process, not a single chemical reaction. Tissue partitioning and energy state prevent a fixed food-to-acetyl-CoA yield. Cofactor participation creates no separate dietary admissions.

evidence.statement: Human medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase establishes the initial beta-oxidation reaction; the clinical exposure additionally measures downstream ketone provision.

transformations.process: Hepatic mitochondrial ketogenesis proceeds through acetoacetyl-CoA formation, HMG-CoA synthase and HMG-CoA lyase to produce acetoacetate.
dependencies: Ketone release, circulation and brain monocarboxylate transport
transformations.limitations: The endogenous product can interconvert with beta-hydroxybutyrate, but the target identity here is acetoacetate. Ketogenesis, cerebral uptake and ATP production are distinct; no fixed yield or universal benefit is inferred.

evidence.statement: Curated human ACAT1, HMGCS2 and HMGCL reactions, retrieved 26 October 2026.

presence_records.label: Sulforaphane
presence_records.public_note: One UK broccoli lot, cooked sous vide at 100 °C for 20 minutes, formed 1.06 µmol sulforaphane per g dry weight. Adding 1 g brown mustard powder raised that to 8.58 µmol/g dry weight. Twelve adults who ate 200 g excreted 9.8 µmol sulforaphane-NAC per g creatinine in 24 hours, and 44.7 µmol/g creatinine with the mustard. These figures are not a sulforaphane amount for every 100 g of broccoli.
presence_records.source_note: Okunade et al. (2018), Molecular Nutrition & Food Research 62:1700980, Table 1 and the 24-hour urine result. Table 1, µmol sulforaphane per g dry weight: raw 2.05 ± 0.25; sous vide 100 °C for 20 minutes 1.06 ± 0.18; the same cooked broccoli plus 1 g brown mustard powder 8.58 ± 0.33. 8.58 / 1.06 = 8.1, which the paper reports as an 8-fold increase. One results sentence prints the mustard result as 8.58 ± 0.13; the table figure is used here. Urine, 12 adults, 200 g of that cooked broccoli: 9.8 ± 5.1 µmol sulforaphane-NAC per g creatinine in 24 hours without mustard, and 44.7 ± 33.9 with 1 g mustard. 44.7 / 9.8 = 4.6 from the published means. The paper's average of each person's increase is 4.7-fold, with individual increases from 1.7-fold to 10-fold. Sous-vide myrosinase loss in the same paper: 40% after 2 minutes, 90% after 6 minutes, and no measurable activity after 8 minutes. The study did not report a glucoraphanin concentration, and the dry-weight results are not converted to a fresh 100 g amount. Fahey et al. (1997) identifies sulforaphane as the myrosinase product of glucoraphanin; it is not the source of these figures.

calculation.not_a_panel_amount: Dry-weight and creatinine-normalised study results. No moisture figure is given, so they are not scaled to per 100 g fresh broccoli.

observations.source_note: DHA varies widely by species and preparation. USDA FoodData Central for "Mollusks, oyster, Pacific, cooked, moist heat" (FDC 174250; via MyFoodData: https://tools.myfooddata.com/nutrition-facts/174250/wt2) implies ~500 mg DHA per 100 g (0.425 g per 85 g). European flat oysters (Ostrea edulis) in the Danish FRIDA database are lower (~193 mg DHA per 100 g raw; Food ID 163: https://frida.fooddata.dk/food/163). Use as an indicative range.

nutrition_value_reviews.title: DHA observation: independent confirmation unresolved
nutrition_value_reviews.description: The archived USDA record reports DHA at 47 mg/100 g. Identity and unit conversion are verified, but independent confirmation of this amount in edible quinoa remains unresolved. The database observation is retained here, not replaced with zero or relabelled as ALA.
nutrition_value_reviews.decision: Temporarily withhold quinoa from DHA food lists and quantified rankings. The former 47 mg omega-3 total depended entirely on this held observation and is withheld too. Unqualified 18:3 remains separately unresolved. Reinstate only after review of supporting analytical identity and food basis.

derived.limitation: The C8 acyl form is not free octanoate content in food. Mixed-chain MCT products have formulation-dependent composition. This is a multireaction biological process, not a single chemical reaction. Tissue partitioning and energy state prevent a fixed food-to-acetyl-CoA yield. Cofactor participation creates no separate dietary admissions. The endogenous product can interconvert with beta-hydroxybutyrate, but the target identity here is acetoacetate. Ketogenesis, cerebral uptake and ATP production are distinct; no fixed yield or universal benefit is inferred.

strategies.label: Minced rather than intact beef in the tested older-adult meal
strategies.limitation: Single crossover with 135 g intrinsically labelled beef. Total plasma EAA concentrations and muscle protein synthesis did not differ detectably. Not a universal meat, protein or neurotransmitter prescription; earlier no-selected-SOP wording records the prior assessment.

strategies.label: Boiled rather than raw eggs in the tested postexercise meal
strategies.limitation: The 45-man trial compared five eggs after resistance exercise; higher peak concentrations did not establish greater brain delivery or a detectable muscle-protein-synthesis advantage.

strategies.label: Tested fish-meal versus fish-oil capsule regimens over 16 weeks
strategies.limitation: Red-cell DHA is peripheral exposure, not neuronal incorporation, cognition or clinical benefit. No detected DHA group difference; nonsignificance is not equivalence. Post-hoc power could not detect RBC EPA+DHA differences below1.5 percentage points. Small unblinded active-comparator study without untreated control; fish adherence self-reported and groups differed in age. Specified albacore tuna, farmed Atlantic salmon and tested DHA-rich capsules; not arbitrary fish/capsule interchangeability. More fishy aftertaste with capsules; lipid changes do not establish cardiovascular benefit.

strategies.label: Limit unnecessary cumulative heat exposure when retaining creatine in pork products
strategies.limitation: Evidence is limited to processed pork matrices and does not establish higher creatine intake or cerebral target engagement.

strategies.label: Steam spinach or broccoli rather than boiling in the tested conditions
strategies.limitation: Controlled food-composition experiment, not a feeding trial. Total folate is not a 5-MTHF quantity. No absorption, tissue flux or clinical outcome was measured; other foods and preparation objectives differ.

strategies.label: Unheated extracted potato resistant-starch supplementation

evidence.finding_role: Mechanistic home only; intervention efficacy and SEC come from the separately cited primary trial, not this Finding.

strategies.limitation: Faecal concentration is not production flux, epithelial exposure or brain signalling. Extracted unheated RS2 supplement; not cooked/cooled potato meals or a verified equivalent banana dose. Maize resistant starch and inulin did not significantly raise butyrate; no alpha-diversity change. Small supplement groups, incompletely masked participants, background diet uncontrolled and sample-completeness exclusions. Individual microbiota-dependent heterogeneity; universal response is unsupported.

strategies.label: Steam spinach or broccoli rather than boiling in the tested conditions
strategies.limitation: Controlled food-composition experiment, not a feeding trial. Total folate is not a 5-MTHF quantity. No absorption, tissue flux or clinical outcome was measured; other foods and preparation objectives differ.

strategies.label: Tested roasted-nori daily protocol
strategies.limitation: Between-group MMA and folate changes were not significant; no significant advantage of 8 over 5 g. Product B12 varies; not all seaweed is equivalent. Did not eliminate deficiency in all participants; no replacement for established deficiency treatment. Small, short, unblinded study; no tissue flux or clinical benefit measured.

strategies.label: Black tea one hour after rather than with an iron-containing porridge meal
strategies.limitation: Small nonrandomised fixed-order study in iron-replete women. No brain iron or dopamine endpoint; not a green-tea or universal timing claim.

strategies.label: Tested malted and soaked oat porridge
strategies.limitation: Pilot-plant malting and controlled soaking are not household overnight oats; acute absorption in ten adults does not establish tissue BHMT flux, long-term zinc status or clinical benefit.

strategies.label: Myrosinase-completed broccoli sprout homogenate
strategies.limitation: This is three days of that homogenate in healthy adults and nasal enzyme RNA, not brain Nrf2, an ordinary broccoli serving, or the four-week sprout-extract capsules that did not raise lung target-gene expression in COPD.

strategies.label: Vinegar with the studied starchy meal
strategies.limitation: Indirect marker in ten healthy volunteers, no appearance flux. Further delay occurred in diabetic gastroparesis and may be disadvantageous; do not apply this practice to that context.

strategies.label: 25 mL/day (22 g) raw olive oil replacing other raw fats; 366 versus 2.7 mg/kg phenolics, with intermediate 164 mg/kg arm; three weeks each, two-week washouts.
strategies.limitation: No claim of reduced inflammatory signalling or universal systemic antioxidant effect. Defined oils; retail EVOO label does not guarantee tested phenolic concentration. Short interventions in healthy men; diet self-report and co-food interactions remain limitations.

searches.finding: Olive-oil HPLC study confirmed. Existing mg/L sample means retained in canonical supplementary records; no mass-density conversion. Pistachio sample range proposed separately.
Purchas et al. measured cooked/uncooked beef and lamb; original numerical table not retrieved. No fabricated universal meat value.
Demarquoy original radioisotopic food analysis located; exact food-specific table unavailable. NIH serving estimate remains explicitly estimated.

USDA release 2 contains betaine and choline moieties. Phosphatidylcholine column is choline contributed by phosphatidylcholine, not phosphatidylcholine molecular mass. No relabelling as PC mg. Exact food/state joins require further reconciliation.
USDA NDB 19165 cocoa quantified; proposed record retains processing and analytical form.
NR and nicotinamide measured in skim milk; nicotinic acid and NAD+ not quantifiable. Do not substitute total niacin or infer NAD+ occurrence.

Original amino-acid database evaluation distinguishes sequence-derived estimates from hydrolysis measurements, which conflate glutamine/glutamate and cystine/cysteine. Exact canonical food, amino-acid form and analytical joins remain unresolved.
Original dehydrated garlic/onion FOS storage study located. Dry solids and chain-length definitions cannot be equated with raw-food values or a combined FOS/GOS protocol. No numerical backfill.
Tested oat malting/soaking supports a bounded presence/protocol proposal, not a generic quantity.
Original isotope-dilution HPLC/MS/MS study located. Vitamer-specific methods support keeping total folate separate; no missing numerical table invented.
